title: Anybody Headed Down Today?
intro: Word is Priya's out on the green in Jefferson, asking if anybody's driving down to the city today. Hannah at Stewart's heard it first.
smallTalk: Priya's kid has a big show in the city tonight — I hope somebody's headed down that way.
Priya's been carrying that costume bag around under one arm all morning.
Tops finally got the good peaches in.
This has been the soggiest summer anybody up here can remember, and everybody's got an opinion about it.
Half the county's heard about Priya's kid's costume bag by now.
Somebody's always driving down to the city, if you ask around enough.
Word travels faster than traffic on Route 10, and that's saying something.
I hope that costume makes it there in one piece — I heard it's got sequins.
Walt's truck could use a wash before it goes anywhere near the city.
Nice to see everybody pitching in for Priya's kid.
Somebody's fixing up the space under Stamford Coffee. Ask ten people what it's going to be and you'll get eleven answers.
There's paper over that low window under the coffee shop now. Whatever's going in, they're keeping it a surprise.
Heard hammering under Stamford Coffee again this morning. Good sound, that — something's coming.
My neighbour says the new place under the coffee shop is a bookshop. My other neighbour says it isn't. Neither of them has been inside.
Stamford Coffee's got a record on and a whole shelf of coffee makers lined up like a museum. Go look, it's worth the trip on its own.
The paninis at Stamford Coffee — get whichever one they're pressing when you walk in. Never been wrong yet.
If you're late getting home, the self-serve fridge at Stamford Coffee has dinner in it. That fridge has saved a lot of Tuesdays.
80 Main's got the Catskills sweaters in again. I'm not saying I need another one. I'm saying I'm going to look.
80 Main had a coffee table made out of coal. Made of coal! I went in twice just to look at it.
Oyster night at 80 Main — get your name down early, it fills right up.
Whatever goes in under the coffee shop, it's got the best patio in town right on top of it. Lucky them.

lines: He texted a photo from the stage door the second he got it — you'll just have to imagine it, but trust me, it's a whole look.
Thank you, truly.
Oh — you were just down in Stamford. Did anybody tell you what's going in under the coffee shop? Nobody will tell me either. I keep hoping dance studio, but I'm biased.
Still asking around? Try the gas station — half the county passes through there before nine.
Renata might know something — Cellar Door, down in Hobart.
Hannah sent you to Stamford Coffee? Go on in — that's where everybody's morning starts, city-bound or not.
Hannah's over at Stewart's, in Stamford — start there if you haven't yet.
My kid's in a dance showcase in the city tonight, and half his costume is in this bag.
I'm due back at the register at Middle Brook by four, or I'd drive it down myself. Here — take it, would you?
If you hear of anybody headed down today, ask them for me. Hannah's behind the counter at Stewart's, down in Stamford; she hears everybody's plans before they make them.
Tell me that bag made it to the stage door in one piece.
Renata sent you to Walt, then — J&H, the gas station up in Jefferson.
Paninis for the road and a bottle from Cellar Door? Then Renata's your next stop — down in Hobart. She'll put a name to that order.
Nobody from in here's going down today, far as I know.
But nobody drives to the city without stopping at Stamford Coffee first — paninis for the road, it's practically a rule. Ask in there, on Main Street. Check the board at Tops on your way, too.

And did you hear? Somebody's fixing up the space under Stamford Coffee. Everybody who comes through that door has a different answer for what it is. Mine's a bookshop, so we'd have one of our own up this end of the road.
Morning! Coffee's on, and the sundae bar's real, if you're curious.
Priya called down from Jefferson asking if anybody's driving to the city today — she's out on the green up there, if you're headed that way.
Glad it worked out. Come by for a tasting sometime, once things settle down.
Go on, catch him before he leaves — the gas station, up in Jefferson.
Two paninis and a cold brew to go, then a bottle from me first thing this morning? Not me — my truck's in the shop. That's Walt.
I saw him loading a cooler bag into his trunk up at the gas station on my way in. Nobody packs a cooler for a trip up the road — that's a city run.
J&H, the gas station up in Jefferson. Go on, catch him before he leaves.
Hannah sent you? Then she'll have said: anybody driving to the city stops at Stamford Coffee first.
Ask in there what got ordered for the road this morning, then come back and tell me. I'll know who it was.
Priya's costume run? Word travels. Not me today — my truck's in the shop.
Ask Hannah at the counter in Stewart's, up in Stamford; she'll know who was in this morning.
Welcome — pull up a seat on the bench anytime.
If you're headed up toward Jefferson, say hi to Priya on the green — I hear she's asking around about something.

And if you pass Stamford Coffee, have a look at the space under it — somebody's putting something in. Hannah says bookshop. I say record shop. Have you seen the wall of LPs upstairs? Something's got to catch the overflow.
Tell the kid break a leg from me. Had it there by six, like I said.
Priya's kid's costume? Sure — I'm headed down myself today, every other Sunday like clockwork.
Hand it over — I've got it. I'll get it to the stage door by six. Tell the kid break a leg.
Heard something's going around about a favor for Priya. Nothing solid on my end, but you never know who overhears what.
Every other Sunday I load up and head down for the week — traffic and all. Don't ask me why I keep doing it to myself.
If you're new around here, Priya's out on the green — good person to know.
Heard about the space under Stamford Coffee? Bike shop. Has to be. All those rail-trail folks rolling into town needing a tube and a coffee — mark my words.
So the paninis were Walt's. Of course they were — every other Sunday, same order. Tell Priya's kid break a leg from the record player's table.
And whatever you've heard about the space underneath us: gallery. Half the people at these tables paint.
Renata, at Cellar Door in Hobart — that's who'll know whose order that was. Whoever it was, they said they were stopping there for a bottle.
And whatever you've heard about the space underneath us: it's a gallery. Half the people at these tables paint. I've seen the sketchbooks.
Priya's costume run? Hannah sent you to the right place. Somebody was in early — two paninis wrapped for the road and a cold brew big enough to get to Brooklyn on.
I didn't catch who; I had my head in the LPs. But they said they were stopping at Cellar Door for a bottle first. Renata will know — down in Hobart.
And while you're here — whatever you've heard about the space underneath us, it's a gallery. Half the people at these tables paint. I've seen the sketchbooks.
You've heard about the space downstairs, then. Well, whatever you were told, it's a gallery. Half the people at these tables paint. I've seen the sketchbooks.
They put paper over the window before I could get a look. I respect that. I'm still going to try.
Sit anywhere — this is the record player's table, so you get whichever side they've put on.
Have you heard? Somebody's doing something with the space underneath us. Hammering all last week. Nobody knows what it is, including the counter, and the counter knows everything.
My money's on a gallery. Half the people at these tables paint. I've seen the sketchbooks.
So you've heard about the downstairs. Everyone's guessing. Oysters — that's my guess and I'm sticking with it. The wine nights in here fill right up; imagine that every night of the week.
Whoever it is, they've picked the best spot in town. Coffee upstairs, sweaters next door. I'd open there.
Don't mind me, I'm deciding between two sweaters and losing.
You've noticed the work going on under the coffee shop? Whole town's noticed. Nobody's got the answer, which hasn't slowed anybody down.
My guess is an oyster bar. The oyster-and-wine nights in here fill right up — somebody's clearly been paying attention.
Somebody's told you about the space under the coffee shop, then. Did they say dog treats? No? Well, it's dog treats. Look at this deck — every dog in Stamford naps here. That's a customer base.
Biscuit here has been sniffing at that papered-over window every walk this week. He knows something. He's not telling either.
Morning. Biscuit likes to check the patio before we go anywhere else, so we check the patio.
Have you heard about the space underneath the coffee shop? Somebody's doing it up. There's paper on the window and hammering behind it, and that's all anybody knows.
My guess is dog treats. Every dog in Stamford naps on this deck. Somebody's finally noticed.

steps.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Taped by the register: "Anybody headed down today? Ask around!" Half the county's already heard.
Pinned to the board by the door: someone's asking if anybody's headed down to the city today. Half the county's seen it already.
Down the side of the coffee shop, a low window right at the ground, with brown paper and a sheet of plywood over it from the inside. Somebody's at work behind it — you can hear a saw going.
Not a word written on any of it. Everybody who walks past leans in for a look anyway, and comes away knowing exactly as much as before.
